question: What will Japan's October 2026 domestic corporate goods price index (CGPI) year-on-year change be?

calls.reasoning: Arithmetic anchor: Sep-2026 index 135.7 (+6.8% y/y); Oct-2025 base rose +0.5% m/m (revised), so a flat Oct-2026 m/m gives ~6.3% y/y. October 2026 drivers: end of Jul-Sep electricity/gas subsidy (high-voltage 1.8 yen/kWh, larger than 2025's subsidy, though the 2025 rate is from memory), WTI up from ~$90-93 at end-Sep to ~$104 at end-Oct, and seasonal October price revisions, offset by falling new-crop rice and a flat yen (~157-158). Net expected m/m about +0.3, giving a median of ~6.6. No consensus published yet; no Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold market found. Forecasters missed September badly (+0.4 expected vs -0.3 actual), so the band is kept wide.
calls.dossier:
- Sep-2026 prelim domestic CGPI (2020=100): 135.7, -0.3% m/m, +6.8% y/y; Aug revised +7.6% y/y; m/m path 2026: May +0.9, Jun +0.4, Jul +0.1, Aug -0.2, Sep -0.3 (minkabu; BoJ release titles). Consensus for Sep was +0.4 m/m / 7.6 y/y, so actual came in far below.
- Oct-2025 base: prelim +0.4% m/m, index 127.5, +2.7% y/y; revised in the Nov-2025 release to +0.5% m/m, +2.8% y/y (so index ~127.6-127.7). Nov-2025 was +0.3% m/m (BoJ cgpi2510/cgpi2511 snippets). Oct-2025 m/m adjusted for summer electricity rates was +0.6 vs +0.4 unadjusted, so the end of summer rates subtracted about 0.2pp, a seasonal effect present in both years.
- Identity: Oct-26 y/y ≈ 6.8 + m/m(Oct-26) - 0.5; flat m/m -> ~6.3. y/y is computed from rounded index levels; Sep-2026 revisions (usually ±0.1-0.2) also feed in.
- Electricity/gas subsidy (METI, Jun 2026): Jul-Sep 2026 usage; high-voltage 1.8/2.3/1.8 yen/kWh, low-voltage 3.5/4.5/3.5; ends with Sep usage, so Oct usage is unsubsidized (upward m/m in Oct). 2025 summer subsidy (from memory, not checked against a source) was smaller: high-voltage ~1.0/1.2/1.0.
- Oil: WTI ~$90.4-92.9 at end-Sep 2026 (above $100 at one point in Sep on a Saudi pipeline attack); ~$98 on Oct 20; ~$104 on Oct 30 (OANDA). Hormuz/Iran tensions. Sep release: imported petroleum/coal/gas +43.6% y/y in yen.
- USD/JPY Oct 2026: 157.7 open, 157.6 close, range 156.1-159.0 (fundamentals.top); Sep saw a 1.5-yen yen appreciation.
- Sep 2026 y/y contributions (NLI): nonferrous +1.57pp, chemicals +1.02pp, petroleum/coal +0.75pp, farm products -0.71pp; farm products -8.8% m/m in Sep (new-crop rice) and -13.3% y/y.
- Mid-Oct AI-stock weakness (risk to nonferrous/copper prices); copper path for October not found.
- BoJ Oct-30 Outlook: oil and AI-related semiconductor demand pushing goods prices up.
- Searched, absent: economist consensus for Oct-2026 CGPI; Oct average of Dubai crude; October copper price.
- Resolves off the BoJ preliminary Oct-2026 release (Nov 12, 2026, 8:50 JST), fixed-base 2020=100 headline y/y; not the chained index or the summer-electricity-adjusted variant.
- Event window: October 2026 price month -> preliminary print Nov 12; as of Nov 2, the month is 100% elapsed, but the data is unpublished.
calls.reference_class: Monthly domestic CGPI m/m changes in 2025-2026 applied to the y/y base-effect identity (y/y_Oct ≈ y/y_Sep + m/m_Oct26 - m/m_Oct25)

calls.reasoning: Base effect: Oct 2025 m/m was +0.4%, so y/y ≈ 6.8 + 1.07*(Oct26 m/m − 0.4) plus revisions. Upside: summer electricity/gas subsidy ended with September usage (high-voltage 1.8 yen/kWh vs 1.5 in 2025), and Brent rose >10% in October (~$113). Offsets: gasoline capped near 170 yen via wholesale subsidy (52.4 yen/L), yen flat (~157.9 vs 157.5), copper −1% in Oct, farm prices falling. Central m/m ~+0.45% → ~6.85-6.9%. Sept's −0.3% was a big downside surprise, so monthly noise is high. No human market or published consensus found (Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold: none).

Assume m/m ~+0.1% +/-0.4 plus slight upward revision bias to Sept. No human market found (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi none).
calls.dossier:
- BoJ Sept 2026 prelim (released 2026-10-13): domestic CGPI 135.7, -0.3% m/m, +6.8% y/y; Aug 2026 -0.2% m/m prelim, y/y 7.6% (minkabu shows revised 7.7). Consensus for Sept had been +0.4% m/m / 7.6% y/y, so the actual came in 0.8pp below (minkabu news 2026-10-13).
- NLI report 2026-10-13: Sept y/y contributions: nonferrous metals +1.57pp, chemicals +1.02pp, petroleum/coal products +0.75pp, agriculture/forestry/fishery -0.71pp; agricultural products incl. rice fell 8.8% m/m and -13.3% y/y (first negative since Apr 2024).
- Base month: BoJ Oct 2025 prelim index 127.5, +0.4% m/m (summer-electricity-adjusted +0.6%), +2.7% y/y (BoJ cgpi2510; Jiji/Nikkei 2025-11-13). minkabu lists the Oct 2025 m/m as revised to +0.5%. Implied Sept 2025 base is about 127.06-127.1, so the revised Oct 2025 level is probably ~127.6-127.7 (not confirmed directly).
- Arithmetic: Oct 2026 y/y ≈ 135.7*(1+m_Oct26)/Oct2025 base - 1; with m=0 that is ~6.26% (base 127.7) to ~6.35% (base 127.6). The Oct release may also revise Sept 2026 (recent revisions have run up to +0.1pp, per minkabu).
- October seasonal: the summer business-electricity rate ends in October, which subtracted ~0.2pp from the Oct 2025 m/m. Past Oct m/m: 2025 +0.4, 2024 ~+0.2, 2023 ~-0.4 (subsidy effects), 2022 ~+0.6.
- Oil: per Bloomberg (2026-10-25 headline/summary), crude eased slightly from a 6-month high on Iran risk, with Brent just under ~$116; Dubai ~112.9 for the week of Oct 25. Monthly Sep average reported at Brent ~116.8 / Dubai ~93.3 by pps-net (data quality uncertain).
- Gasoline/diesel/kerosene/heavy-oil subsidy: 42.4 yen/L (Oct 8-14), 42.8 (Oct 22-28), a record 52.4 from Oct 29; pump price held around 170 yen. This caps wholesale petroleum product prices. Phase-down from December is proposed, not decided.

- Sept 2026 import prices +24.5% y/y in yen terms; imported petroleum/coal/gas +43.6% y/y (question background).
- Status quo: y/y has run 6.3-7.6% since May 2026 (May 6.3, Jun 7.1, Jul 7.2, Aug 7.6, Sep 6.8).
- Market check: none found on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi. A private-economist consensus for October was not yet published as of 2026-11-02.

calls.reasoning: Oct-2025 base index is 127.6 (revised +0.5% m/m), so flat Oct-2026 m/m gives 135.7/127.6-1 = 6.35% (prints 6.3). The Jul-Sep 2026 electricity subsidy (high-voltage 1.8 yen/kWh in Sep) was larger than 2025's (1.0), so its end adds roughly 0.1pp more than in Oct 2025. Brent rose >10% in October and lagged fuel-cost adjustments are high. Offsets: the gasoline subsidy rising to 52.4 yen/L, falling new-crop rice, copper -1%, a flat yen. Central m/m ~+0.35% -> ~6.7% y/y. Width reflects the large September surprise. No human market or published consensus found.
calls.reconciliation: Factual 1: Oct-2025 base. Run 2 used +0.4% m/m; Runs 1 and 3 used revised +0.5%. My search returned a BoJ source snippet giving the Oct-2025 index as 127.6 (+0.5% m/m), so flat Oct-2026 gives 6.35% (prints 6.3). Run 2's base assumption was too high. Factual 2: 2025 summer subsidy. METI's page confirms high-voltage 1.0/1.2/1.0 yen/kWh for Jul-Sep 2025 usage. That matches Run 1's memory; Run 2's 1.5 is wrong. Against 2026's 1.8, the Oct-2026 subsidy roll-off adds ~0.8 yen/kWh more than in 2025, roughly +0.1pp on CGPI. Judgment: size of Oct m/m. Weighing the oil rise and subsidy roll-off against the gasoline cap, rice and copper, I take ~+0.35% m/m -> median 6.7, between Run 3 (6.4) and Run 2 (6.87). Run 3's dispersion is carried forward, slightly narrowed. No market found; none needed for blending.
